So the earlier 0/10 was INFEASIBILITY, NOT DIFFICULTY. Cause: the physics leaves essentially one way to do it (the cranking ladder forces the unit order, the minimum-output corridor forces load pickup, step pacing is mechanical), so a 73-action plan is 73 FORCED actions -- the opposite of the feasibility-coupled long object that makes search hard. **DROPPED** before building. see task-src/black-start/SPIKE.md |

KILLED by gate B: on witness-generated (provably feasible) instances a ~40 line randomized greedy multistart solved **36/36 at the EXACT optimum** (cost == LB) in 1-76 restarts at every tightness that is feasible at all, n=120/k=10 and n=300/k=16 alike. CAUSE: the move graph is COMPLETE, so free space is fungible and teleports in one hop -- the sliding-puzzle intuition needs restricted adjacency and there is none. Instances are therefore bimodal with nothing between: total free below the largest moving shard = INFEASIBLE for everyone (the first generator produced these, which is why all planners 'failed' at first and looked like a cliff), above it = a cascade exists and restarts find it. Optimum == LB essentially always, so no cost bar separates. TRANSFERABLE LESSON: the CPU-cap spine only prices out blind search when ONE candidate evaluation is expensive relative to the cap; here a full plan replay costs ~5ms so 8s buys thousands of tries. 3 reference planners built (greedy+min-park, recursive make-room, journaled make-room with rollback) and ALL THREE were beaten by the naive multistart. see task-src/shard-rebalance/SPIKE.md |

Discovery 1 = the bound is PER FRAME so a global amplitude is pinned by the near-silent gap ~30x below what the rest of the piece carries, enough that the baseline does not decode even a CLEAN file. Discovery 2 = 10 of 12 graded chains contain a resample. Stopping after the first is natural (clean decodes, ~1/3 of battery passes). FLOOR UNDER DISCOVERY 2, each a structural failure hit during authoring: (a) full-rate PN gives a 3-sample correlation peak vs ~900 samples of drift, so chips are needed (shipped, not the agent's problem); (b) scoring candidates by raw peak height picks the end of the grid because each candidate leaves a different block count -- must be peak-over-background (chains 3 and 6 failed on this); (c) a resampling error BOTH shifts block k by k*L*d AND rescales time within each block, so a phase ramp models the first only and a coarse resample grid the second only -- reference needs both (ramp alone lost wide ratios, coarse grid alone lost ratios off-grid by 1e-4). ANTI-CHEAT THAT MATTERED: the leave-a-note cheat first scored 12/60 because /tmp is shared between the embed and extract children and setting TMPDIR is not enough (a module writes the literal path). Fixed: scratch root moved to /grading, embed phase dir deleted before the extract child exists, /app + /tmp + /var/tmp + /dev/shm wiped between phases, extract module copied from a pristine root-only copy so a module that rewrites its own file cannot carry the edit across. Re-verified IN THE CONTAINER: 0/60, all sixty returned 0. Other cheats 0: loud stamp (bound 0/5, worst 238x), untouched-carrier-plus-constant (payloads distinct so a constant can be right at most once), dc-offset side channel (bound inf). | view-budget | Software | $175 | SPIKE FIRST, unmeasured | high | high | CLAIM 2026-07-30 07:1x. Difficulty engine = exact output under a hard WORK BUDGET (the reactive-spreadsheet engine, measured in band), NOT a metered clone: line-blame and match-cert already claimed the clone family this morning. Idea: environment ships a bespoke relational view language over bag semantics with the awkward operators (anti-join, outer join, min/max aggregates, a running rank) plus a full recompute reference the agent can call freely, and a stream of base table deltas; the agent must emit exact view contents after every delta while an instrumented harness counts tuples touched, and the budget sits far below full recompute. KILL GATES TO MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING: (A) full recompute vs correct incremental maintenance must differ by >=20x on realistic deltas, (B) the obvious middle strategies (dirty marking, memoised recompute of changed views only) must ALSO blow the budget, else the bar separates clever from dumb rather than clever from obvious, (C) min/max on delete and anti-join retraction must be the part that forces real derivation rather than a textbook counting algorithm. | spiking |
| view-budget (spiked) | Software | $175 | GATES MEASURED, honest | high | high | KILL GATES PASS. First spike measured a strawman (the incremental strategy quietly skipped the rank view); rewritten so the incremental side maintains ALL five views and is asserted equal to a full recompute after every one of 200 deltas. Then: full 815475 units (150x), dirty-downstream 799991 (147x), keyed-region 276735 (51x), correct incremental 5427 (1x). So the bar separates clever from OBVIOUS, not clever from lazy, which is the gate causal-probe failed. Precedent: reactive-spreadsheet, same engine (exactness plus a work bar that blocks recompute-everything), measured 3/8 IN BAND; different shape here (write the maintenance from scratch vs repair a planted bug) so not a near duplicate. METERING DESIGN DECISION: do NOT meter store reads or bytecode. Both are dodgeable, store reads because the agent may cache the base tables in its own state at setup and then recompute privately for free, bytecode because one sorted() call does a whole region of work in a single op. Instead scale the data and the delta stream and let a hard CPU limit in the verifier be the bar: at 150x, full recompute cannot fit and correct incremental maintenance fits with a wide margin, and the limit is enforced by the OS rather than by instrumentation the agent can route around. | spiked, build next |

At the shipped width 48: 1e15 and 1e16 in 0.2s, 1e17 in 2.6s through 5 rebases, 1e18 in 26s through 60. Design changed from a wrapping counter to a REBASE (fill the header field -> halve the whole table), which is lossy (counts one apart become equal) and instantaneous, so it is exactly fast-forwardable, unlike the wrap whose post-event transient runs ~2^bits erases with an order change every period. FIVE debugging rounds were needed and each is a mistake the task would punish: drift taken modulo the field (a rebase is not a translation), taking the shortest repeat rather than the useful one (post-rebase the useful cycle is the COMPOSITE of two alternating patterns, period 10496 uniform drift 90), and re-searching instead of walking the post-rebase transient. **HOLE FOUND BEFORE BUNDLING**: the mechanism is WIDTH INDEPENDENT. erase_bits is a constant in the engine but the agent has the engine and can edit it, and at 8 bits the store rebases every ~128 erases, so the whole pipeline can be built and validated exhaustively against brute force in seconds and then applied at 48 bits. That is a complete local oracle by scale-down -- it is exactly how I built the reference -- so under effort-difficulty-does-not-clear-the-bar this lands too_easy. The wrap design shared the hole. CANDIDATE FIX, needs its own spike: make the dynamics depend on counter MAGNITUDE and not only on differences, via float64 precision loss as counts approach 2^53, which small counters cannot reproduce at all. | paused, hole found |

Three real code paths in tiled.c - lane_span dropping the mask write so padded lanes fold in (tail <= 8 lanes AND k tail 1..3 AND heads % 8 == 0), the split-K drain issuing the hanging partial twice (odd partial count >= 5 AND seq_q % 256 == 0 AND lane tail != 0 AND odd batch), and the single q tile path broadcasting batch 0 (seq_q < 16 AND batch > 1 AND seq_k % 96 == 0). **TWO DEFECTS THE BUILD CAUGHT AND FIXED, BOTH WORTH KEEPING.** (1) The first fold accumulated in uint32 and was multiplied by the tile element count, whose trailing zeros threw away low bits, so distinct sums COLLIDED - 3 of 4000 labels disagreed with the predicate. Widened to a 64 bit accumulator and the collisions went. (2) **The cheat suite caught the real one: `offbyone` (lane_tail <= 9 instead of <= 8) SCORED 1.** The near-miss generator was breaking every clause of a condition at once, so no held shape ever tested a lane tail of 9 with the other clauses satisfied. Rewritten to break EXACTLY ONE CLAUSE per negative; after that offbyone scores 0. That is the generalisable rule for any boundary-graded set: **a negative must violate one clause and satisfy the rest, or the boundary is never tested.** GATES: oracle 1.000 from source AND from the extracted zip, nop 0.000 both, 6 of 6 cheats 0.000 with control 1.000 (always False, always True, off-by-one on the lane tail, the fuzz-fitted approximation, shelling out to the two binaries, forged reward with a rewriter left behind). VERIFIER ISOLATION: agent code runs in a subprocess via tests/runner/ask.py with /tmp as cwd, one shape per line in and one character out, labels never leave the parent, reward from pytest's exit code. Two cheats closed STRUCTURALLY: the verifier image carries only the declared artifact so /app/ref and /app/tiled do not exist at grading time, and no held shape is in the agent container in any form. simscan over 380 bundles: prose cosine max 0.044, 4-gram max 0.280, manifest 0.385 (inflated - tail-lane has only 15 files so the mandatory scaffolding dominates the Jaccard). Round 1 died at quality_check on FIVE criteria, the serious one being a REAL ANSWER LEAK I shipped: sim reads were named <haplotype>:<true-coord>:<i> (A0/A1/B0a/B1/B0dup/U) and the names survived into the BAM, so `samtools view | cut -f1` plus a per-tag consensus reproduced all 100 truth genotypes with zero CNV reasoning. Fixed by shuffling the read pool and naming RUN1:<serial> after the shuffle (emission order leaks the same grouping the names no longer do). Round 2 then passed structure/ai/similarity/oracle_nop/quality/cheat_probe and died at easiness. **THE LESSON IS SCREEN 4, NOT THE DATA.** The DATA was bespoke (reviewer passed `novel` on exactly that) but the METHOD is textbook: paralogy is visible in the shipped reference, the CN step is one `samtools depth`, and `freebayes --ploidy N` is standard practice. Bespoke data on a standard method is NOT a bespoke problem. A multi-step chain where every step is routine is a 10 minute job for a frontier agent no matter how badly naive pipelines score - my measured ladder (60/90/100) only ever proved NAIVE approaches fail, and never tested how fast a competent agent finds the right path. MEASURE TIME-TO-SOLVE, NOT THE NAIVE GAP. | BUILT 2026-08-13, ALL LOCAL GATES GREEN (oracle 1.000 x4 repeatable, nop 0.000, 5 cheats all 0; harbor check NOT RUN, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on this box). MEASURED DIFFICULTY LADDER: standard bcftools/freebayes diploid pipeline 62/100 sites; bcftools with ploidy 3 ABORTS on assert(ploidy<=2) in mcall.c; freebayes ploidy 3 across all of locus 2 (spots the CNV but not the breakpoints) 88/100; correct per segment ploidy 2/3/2 = 100/100. All or nothing grading means the 88/100 near miss scores identically to doing nothing. FIRST TASK UNDER THE REAL-TOOL ANCHORING RULE, and the first genomics task on this account or the old one (corpus grep for samtools/bcftools/pysam/variant/genotype/BAM/VCF returns 0), so the similarity lane is clean. MECHANISM: locus A (2 copies, the panel target) has a 99.2% identical paralog B elsewhere on the contig, and B carries an EXTRA copy on one haplotype (3 copies total). Reads from B mismap into A. Standard practice (bwa mem, bcftools mpileup/call, MAPQ filter) assumes the mismapping background is diploid, so B's third copy skews apparent allele fraction at paralogous sequence variant sites into exactly the range that reads as a real het in A. Agent must notice the duplication (self-align the shipped FASTA with a real tool), infer B's copy number from depth and PSV allele fraction, and only then separate true A variants from B-derived artifacts. WHY IT SURVIVES THE SCREENS: no free oracle (truth is sealed, nothing locally checkable tells them if a call is right); failure is BINARY not a quality metric (exact genotype set); scaffolding is SHIPPED (reference, BAM, index, panel BED, real callers all present, no reimplementation); the problem class is real (SMN1/SMN2, CYP2D6, PMS2) but the locus, the CN configuration and the variant set are bespoke so no published recipe lands it. RISK TO WATCH: MAPQ filtering alone must NOT recover truth - verify empirically before shipping. |

ALL PUBLISHED has no fork left in it, only careful engineering, and careful engineering is eight
minutes for a frontier agent no matter how exact the grading is. I bet the difficulty on the agent

public spec, note.md stated the operational half outright, and the reference converter is ~200 lines.

right answer hard to find. Ablation depth (9 flips, each fatal) measured DISCRIMINATION, not

and departure time per working, so even the sheet parsing was gone. **DO NOT retry this core problem
by making the data messier or the network bigger** - that is more clerical work at the same depth.

format-parity) and genuine off-support extrapolation; the tool anchoring rule constrains WHICH tool,
not WHERE the difficulty comes from, and those two are compatible with anchoring. Bank what DID work:
**the tool-anchored bundle shape cleared similarity three times running, twice with a near-identical
deleted predecessor behind it**, on an account and a lane where the rulebook-reconstruction shape was
blocked five times. Anchor the next Operations idea on a real tool AND put the difficulty in a
metered or extrapolative medium.

## fenwick-verify (Software/Languages) — building 2026-09-12
Dafny 4.11.0 deductive-verification task. CORE PROBLEM: prove functional correctness of a
Fenwick tree / binary indexed tree (query reads back true prefix sum; point update preserves
the tree invariant). Difficulty is the two-adic lowbit duality (descent cells partition 1..k;
ascent cells are exactly the cover of i) — SMT (Z3) cannot close it; needs a hand-built

Chosen after frame-pin died at easiness 3/3. Requirements it must meet, all derived from that post mortem: (a) 15-25 INDEPENDENT all-or-nothing decisions, not 5 coupled ones; (b) deliverable measured in hundreds of graded values, not one 200 line file; (c) it must survive [[free-oracle-screen]], which leaves only two un-banned escapes, feasibility SEARCH at the floor and off-support extrapolation, since metered-clone is a banned family here; (d) **its dominant risk must be measurable WITHOUT an agent trial, because this box has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and easiness cannot be measured locally.** Search is chosen over extrapolation precisely because of (d): if an off the shelf tool cracks the instances, I can find that out myself in an hour. SHAPE: produce inputs that drive a REAL library to k named hard to reach branches, graded by running the real binary under real coverage instrumentation, all or nothing over k. Checking a candidate is free (that is fine, remat-schedule proves the oracle may certify arrival), finding is the work, and deep branches behind long chains of structured input checks are exactly what defeats a fuzzer and needs reasoning. THE SPIKE, before any bundle: pick the real library, pick candidate targets, then run AFL++ or libFuzzer against them for an hour and DROP every target the fuzzer reaches on its own. Anchoring stays honest: the library and the coverage tooling are upstream, only the target set and the harness are bespoke. Obfuscation is NOT a lever, it is a banned source of difficulty. | **DIRECTION KILLED 2026-09-13 BY THE SPIKE, before any bundle was built.** Measured on sqlite 3.50.4 amalgamation built with gcc --coverage, harness opens a db read only and runs integrity_check plus two schema reads. Baseline corpus of 12 valid dbs (plain, index, WITHOUT ROWID, blob overflow, page_size 512 and 65536, auto_vacuum, triggers+views, UTF-16le, foreign keys, empty) covers 3857 branch outcomes of 32172. **A DUMB RANDOM MUTATION FUZZER, 25000 mutants in 209 SECONDS, ADDED 715 NEW BRANCH OUTCOMES.** No coverage feedback, no AFL, just byte flips and interesting-value splats on the corpus. That is the whole objection: an agent's first move on a reach-this-branch task is to run a fuzzer, and on a format whose deep paths are guarded by cheap integer checks on header fields, hundreds of targets fall out for free in the time the easiness probe allows. Of the 27600 still uncovered, only 725 sit on assert/testcase/coverage macros, so 26875 look like real code, but that number is an ARTIFACT OF A NARROW HARNESS: the bulk is in select.c 1958, json.c 1779, where.c 1720, expr.c 1582, reachable by simply running SQL rather than by crafting a file. btree.c, the actual file format core, holds 2033 and most of those need writes. So the honest target yield is small, and proving any candidate is both REACHABLE and FUZZ IMMUNE costs an AFL++ campaign plus a hand construction per target, times 20. **GENERALISABLE LESSON: any reach-this-state-in-a-real-program task is fuzzer vulnerable whenever the guards are cheap integer or byte checks. Fuzz immunity needs SELF CONSISTENCY guards, CRC32 chunks, cross referenced offset tables, abbrev graphs, so that random mutation is almost surely rejected upstream of the target. sqlite is the wrong host precisely because it is designed to detect corruption cheaply.** Candidate hosts if this shape is ever revisited: zip central directory, png chunk CRCs, DWARF abbrev and offset graph, pdf xref. Spike lives at /var/tmp/spike-cov. | killed by spike, data recorded |

fields are direct identifiers (full suppress), which are quasi-identifiers (generalize for

TARGET k ~= 15 masking decisions. This is the proven forced-consequences difficulty mechanism (the
one fenwick lacked). DELIVERABLE: masked dataset, all-or-nothing over cells.
ANCHOR: real formats (CSV/JSON/parquet + SQLite) + real reacting consumers (SQLite GROUP BY
k-anonymity check, Python/pandas utility check, a format/regex validator, referential-consistency

## exec-truth (Software / Systems, $300) — building 2026-09-16 [fresh substrate: dpkg/apt-secure/proc live-state forensics; 0 catalogue hits for dpkg/.deb/debsums/proc-maps]
anchor: dpkg 1.21 (dpkg-deb, dpkg-divert, dpkg file lists/status/diversions), apt-secure repo chain (apt-ftparchive Release + detached gpg), gpgv 2.2, binutils/ELF, Sleuth Kit mactime body format, /proc/<pid>/maps.
CORE (fresh vs catalogue: not a policy verdict-set, not a metered probe, not infer->solve): establish what a captured host is ACTUALLY running versus what its records claim, and split the answer into two coupled exact sets - on-disk paths whose bytes are not the authentic content of the installed version (`reinstall`), and running pids whose MAPPED code is not that authentic content (`restart`). The same authentic-content resolution feeds both, so one resolution error flips items in both sets.
WHY THE NAIVE READING IS CONFIDENTLY WRONG (the license-reach lever):
 - debsums/md5sums lie: the attacker rewrote /var/lib/dpkg/info/*.md5sums to match the tampered file, and md5sums has no entry for symlinks at all.
 - needrestart/`lsof +L1` "(deleted) => restart" is wrong BOTH ways: a package reinstall that changed the inode but not the bytes is deleted-but-clean, and an in-place byte patch (same inode, no marker) is the one that really is running tampered code.
 - path->package is not the dpkg file list: /var/lib/dpkg/diversions reroutes ownership, so the authentic bytes must come from the diverting package's .deb.
 - the repo is not trustworthy by default: one pool .deb disagrees with its Packages SHA256, and one version exists in two suites with different content, settled only by which Release signature verifies under a key valid at that Release date.
AXIS CROSSINGS (not independent readings): conffile x diversion (a conffile of A diverted to B where it is not a conffile, so the conffile exemption does not apply), version x diversion (a diverted path left at the old version by an upgrade), repo-integrity x version (authentic bytes only in the archive suite), live-vs-disk (authentic old inode mapped while the disk holds tampered bytes -> restart NO, reinstall YES; and the mirror image of it), data-vs-code mapping (a drifted read-only data mapping is not a restart).
FREE-ORACLE screen: reading (records lie at every layer), running (the host is a snapshot, nothing to re-run), fuzzing (no differential rig), checking (no oracle says a set is right) all fail.
RISK: readable-substrate easiness death is the standing risk for every non-metered build here; mitigated by making no fact stated (inode identity, hardlink survival and repo authenticity all inferred) and by two-sided crossings rather than independent per-file rules. Author Shaswat Panda.
status: building task-src/exec-truth/.

REAL JOB: a security team audits a fleet of eBPF programs deployed on a locked-down production
host and must decide which programs violate the org kernel-capability policy (KCAP-1). Real tools:
clang/LLVM 21 BPF target (compile the .o with BTF), bpftool 7.7 (btf/prog/map inspection), 
llvm-objdump (disassemble bytecode + read relocations), libbpf headers (map/helper macros). The
fleet ships as REAL compiled .o objects + a human deployment manifest (yaml) + POLICY.md.

CORE (fresh vs whole submitted set - 0 bpf/ebpf hits): reconstruct each program's EFFECTIVE
kernel-capability exposure from the COMPILED BYTECODE (helper `call` immediates, map-fd
relocations, and the tail-call PROG_ARRAY wiring encoded as `__array` initializers in the object's
.maps section relocations/BTF), propagate exposure along the tail-call reachability CLOSURE and
across shared maps, then judge against the bespoke KCAP-1 tier x helper x map-sharing x grant
policy. The deployment manifest LIES both ways (understates helpers, misstates attach hook, hides
map sharing, claims false wiring), so the naive read is two-sided wrong; the truth is only in the
bytes.

WHY IT RESISTS (license-reach recipe, the confirmed non-metered passer): (1) bespoke policy, not
textbook helper-danger recall; (2) records LIE - manifest disagrees with the object both ways;
(3) discriminating evidence (real wiring, real helper set) DISCOVERED from relocations/bytecode,
not read off a column; (4) STRUCTURAL propagation (tail-call closure + shared-map dataflow) so a
per-program single-axis read (p~1) misses the violations that only appear through the wiring =
the revoke-scope band lever, on a NON-readable binary substrate (unlike dnssec-chain which died
readable). Free-oracle screen: reading lies, running gives kernel-safety not policy, nothing to
fuzz, no oracle confirms a candidate set.

FAILURE MODE targeted: the agent trusts the manifest / judges each program independently and
misses exposure that only exists through the compiled tail-call wiring + shared maps.

VERIFIER SHAPE:
anchor: clang/LLVM 21 BPF target + bpftool 7.7 + llvm-objdump + libbpf | agent writes
/app/findings.json {"violations":[prog_id,...]}; verifier bakes the sealed set, runs NO agent
code, checks exact two-sided set match (all-or-nothing) and re-derivable from /app objects only.

scores: difficulty high (biased hard, structural crossings) / verifiability high (exact sealed
set) / specificity high (absolute path, exact contract). status: BUILT, all local gates green (oracle=1 x3 incl extracted zip, nop=0, 4 cheats=0), HELD for manual submit 2026-09-16.

UPDATE 2026-09-16 (7) — dpkg-process-forensics v6 FAILED quality `test instruction alignment` on a
REAL GRADING BUG of mine, caught by the reviewer: pid 381 was on the sealed restart list and should
not have been.
ROOT CAUSE: /proc maps record the path the KERNEL arrived at after walking every link. The
/usr/lib/fleet -> /opt/fleet/lib directory link added in v4 was handled on the DISK side (snap()
walks paths component-by-component) but never on the MAPS side. So a mapping came back as
/opt/fleet/lib/ledger, matched no dpkg .list, fell into the "code no package accounts for" branch
and was flagged -- though its recovered content is byte-identical to the signed fleet-ledger_2.4.
A correct solver would submit 9 pids and fail. Pid 430 was flagged for the same wrong reason and
happened to be right, which is how it hid.
FIX: undirect() maps resolved paths back to the declared name using the collected tree's own
directory links, restricted to links whose target IS A DIRECTORY (otherwise /bin/sh -> /bin/dash and
friends cause wrong rewrites). Exactly one alias in this corpus. Sealed answer now 13 paths, 9 pids.
Map-less fairness proof re-run: still agrees with the real maps exactly.
THE BUG WAS INFLATING DIFFICULTY. It shipped in v4 and v5, so "too hard" on v4 and the measured 0/8
on v5 were PARTLY AN ARTIFACT -- correct solvers were being marked wrong. v5's true difficulty is
unmeasured. v7 keeps all four of v6's published rungs anyway, because too-hard is the more expensive
failure to repeat and erring easy costs the cheaper probe.
ALSO FIXED (advisory `reviewable`): every number in the three explanations is now MEASURED from the
corpus by dev/facts.py, not hand-written. Three were stale (twelve paths vs thirteen, two
unlinked-but-clean processes vs seven, ten pids vs nine).
The bug is now a measured ablation row of its own (+1 pid). 19 ablations, 18 fail.

## pooled-session-isolation (Software / Databases, $300) - BUILT 2026-09-16, local gates green

CORE PROBLEM, subject stripped: *adjudicate a published behavioural contract against a metered
black box, and file an executable counterexample for every clause the box breaks.* Not a
reconstruction of hidden state, not a minimal edit, not a quotient, not a verdict set over a
shipped corpus. The deliverable is fourteen classifications plus five replayable traces, and the
verifier holds no answer key for the witness side: it replays what the report filed and derives
the verdict side by driving the shipped engine.

SUBJECT: an "Edgeline" SQL-over-HTTP pooling appliance, a real PostgreSQL 16.4 cluster behind a
pooling front end in a compose sidecar. Fourteen published session isolation guarantees, nine of
which hold. Every leak is produced by genuine PostgreSQL reset semantics (DISCARD TEMP vs
DEALLOCATE ALL vs RESET ALL vs pg_advisory_unlock_all), not by a simulator.

THE FIVE BREAKS, each conjunctive, each with a SILENT self-consistent trap on the naive probe:
- EDG-4 settings: reset is a hand written list of standard parameters -> `app.*` survives.
  Trap: probing with statement_timeout shows a clean reset.
- EDG-3 identity: connection_id is a hash of the session NAME, not the connection.
  Trap: the appliance's own telemetry says two sessions never shared a connection.
- EDG-5 temp objects: DISCARD TEMP skipped when the last call failed.
  Trap: creating the table and failing in the SAME call rolls it back, so the obvious probe is clean.
- EDG-7 advisory locks: lock sweep dropped while the pool is full (>=3 busy at release).
  Trap: a session that lands ON the leaking connection is granted the lock again and reads
  "released" - my own systematic matrix fell into this and scored the leak as clean.
- EDG-2 affinity: an idle session's connection goes back into circulation, name kept.
  Trap: with a quiet pool it is handed the same connection back. And EDG-11 (reclaim never touches
  an OPEN TRANSACTION) genuinely holds, so testing reclaim the scary way hides EDG-2 completely.
NEAR MISSES: prepared statements (EDG-6) and sequence position (EDG-8) are swept on EVERY path, so
concluding by family rather than by measurement is wrong in both directions.

CALIBRATION (measured, not assumed, per [[calibrate-against-the-route-the-agent-takes]]):
- reference route 82 billed calls of 180, honest discovery, no constants.
- SYSTEMATIC MATRIX route (dev/matrix_probe.py, 7 kinds of session state x 5 release conditions):
  **203 calls - over the allowance - and it catches only 2 of the 5.** That is what 180 is set
  against, not a strawman.
- six wrong reports all measured at reward 0, including three with CORRECT classification and the
  naive trace shape for temp / locks / affinity.

INFO DENIAL, the mechanism that has cleared this account's easiness probe: metered per call
(refused calls billed, no top up) AND the application role has no catalog or cluster introspection
(25 escalation/introspection attempts measured denied, incl. pg_backend_pid, pg_stat_activity,
pg_locks, pg_class, information_schema, to_reg*, COPY FROM PROGRAM, CREATE EXTENSION). So which
physical connection a statement ran on is not a question the database will answer - the settings
leak is the only handle, which makes the first defect the instrument for finding the rest.

GATES: harbor oracle 1.000 (8m07s), harbor nop 0. Verifier 35 tests: 5 reference traces, 13 upheld
probes under the breaking conditions, 8 lookalike traces the detectors must stay QUIET on, plus
shape and grading. harbor check not runnable locally (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, per [[humanizer-dead]]
note on this account).

BUG CAUGHT LATE, worth remembering: the affinity detector counted backends per session NAME, so a
trace that closed a session and reused the name fired EDG-2 with no violation. Fixed by giving each
session an incarnation epoch and keying the detector on (name, epoch), and locked in as a lookalike
probe. Audit every detector for "what non-violation could produce this signal".

**COLLISION FOUND AFTER BUILD (2026-09-16).** `delivery-guarantee-audit`, built the SAME DAY in a
parallel session on this account, has the SAME CORE: metered black box + per-clause adjudication
of a shipped contract + replayable witnesses on a fresh copy + role-based info denial +

  suppresses single/pair flips: lock1 singles [.05,.05,.04] pairs [.17-.26]. Calibrating full-flip
  >=0.98 (lock1 undertrained at 0.65; bd1 0.82). Trigger tokens must be DISTINCTIVE mid-freq real
  words (common filler words -> weak ASR + spurious rare-token triggers).

LAYERS (a sidecar retry multiplies an application-client retry), retry budgets/throttles are INERT for a single
cold request (naive application undercounts), hedging amplifies even on success, retryable-status sets decide
whether a hop retries at all, and deadline propagation decides whether the client sees DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or the
upstream status while orphaned work continues.

edge extraction over-counts fanout; configured attempt counts must come from config, the topology from traces.

distinct from weaken-atomics (a race it cannot see), column-impact (value invariance), malloc-acceptance (test
adequacy), license-reach (an induced rule).

### column-impact v3 (2026-09-21) — v2 passed easiness AND difficulty, died RUN AUDIT
v2 cleared seven gates including the difficulty probe, then failed the run audit on `task
specification` 5 of 8 trials. Agents reached 1414/1420 entries with zero false positives and lost on
the same six entries in the same three projects: `WHERE <expr> IS NOT NULL` where the expression is a
SUBSTR or a subtraction over a masked column. The reference collapsed every property of a derived
expression and called the null pattern lost; the agents applied ordinary SQL null-strictness and were
right. LESSON: when the deliverable is "not guaranteed", a CONSERVATIVE rule is as unfair as a wrong
one, and the judge reads the trajectories and sees the agent arguing correctly against you. A
soundness check only tests one direction; you must also be able to demonstrate every claimed change.
v3 fixes null-strict propagation (slices, differences, concatenation, arithmetic, casts, functions,
aggregates; COALESCE never-null only against a literal fallback), states the standard in the rules
("guaranteed under ordinary SQL evaluation"), adds a hard check that every claimed row-set move is
seen on data, and adds five unambiguous distinctions to take up the slack the fix leaves: a
merging-method join that gains matches, a slice inside vs past a truncation, CASE WHEN x IS NULL, a
two-column fallback, and a report grouped by a slice. 36 projects, 1282 models, 1603 entries, 915
columns reached-but-intact, 24 readings ablated and 23 silently wrong. oracle 1.000 / nop 0.000 from
the extracted zip; 15 cheats 0; sqlite zero disagreements. HELD for manual submit.

### column-impact v4 (2026-09-21) — v3 cleared the audit then DIED EASINESS 2/3
The v3 fairness fix removed a rule that had been holding the difficulty up, so the task fell below
the bar. LESSON: when an audit says a rule was wrong, the difficulty it was providing is gone too;
replace it in the same pass. v4 turns the pre-registered dial — a sixth method (`bucket`, round down
to a multiple, where a bound ON a rounding edge still decides the same rows and one off it does not)
and six composition rules about provenance surviving operations: MIN/MAX/AVG of a fixed-offset
column keep that offset so the span between two of them is unchanged, while SUM does not; a constant
added to such a column keeps the offset; LAG/LEAD is the same column so a row-to-row gap survives; a
fallback between two columns under one key is still that column; a cast or constant fallback does not
stop a rounding edge deciding a bound. Account key pseudonymised consistently across five landing
tables. 36 projects, 1432 models, 1555 files, 1.10 MB, answer 2453 entries, 1003 columns
reached-but-intact, 31 readings ablated and 29 silently wrong (the six new ones at 14-21 projects

anchor: real Redpanda 24.2.7 (Kafka API) broker sidecar + real librdkafka clients via confluent-kafka 2.6.1 (murmur2 partitioner, consumer groups, auto.offset.reset, metadata refresh, auto-commit) + rpk | verifier grades ONLY an HMAC-signed record the sealed services keep of themselves (per-account generated / applied / sequence jumps / owed / per-partition counts, partition count, ingest state) fetched by a main-service collect hook after a 120 s soak; runs no agent code.
CORE PROBLEM, subject stripped: *change the sharding of a live keyed stream without any reader ever seeing one key out of order or missing a record, when every client on the stream learns about shards differently and the change cannot be undone.* ONE-SHOT LIVE OPERATION family; the only submitted relative is hot-reshape (Postgres expand/contract, dropped at similarity before any other gate). jwks-rotate / lease-fence / flash-sale-rca are held and unsubmitted.
FAILURE MODE (fresh for the submitted list): an invariant the agent does not preserve + a race it cannot see. Key->partition = hash mod N, so raising N re-homes most keys the instant a producer refreshes metadata; anything unprocessed in the old partition is overtaken.
WHY NOT the ideas screened out the same session: semantic merge (diskcache-fork-merge died easiness 3/3 twice), crash bucketing without labels (collides with submitted crash-bucket), min-churn CVE lockfile remediation (solver-mappable lazy-ILP + same min-cost-under-budget template as weaken-atomics/reg-budget), entity resolution (record linkage blocked at similarity 4x), FK discovery (not uniquely determined), canary verdicts (same core as perf-regression-triage).
SILENT, TWO-SIDED TRAPS, each a consequence the agent must INFER from real client settings (nothing states it):
- applier: auto.offset.reset=latest + 5 min metadata refresh -> discovers new partitions after ingest writes to them and skips those events (measured on the real stack in the spike: 699 events skipped, zero errors anywhere) -> must be restarted between alter and resume, and hold a committed position on all 24.
- indexer: enable.auto.commit=true + partition-affine bulk workers flushing every 75 s -> group lag reads 0 while it still holds up to 75 s of events; the drain barrier is its own pending counter. Restarting it DISCARDS that batch (offsets already committed) -> over-restarting fails.
- audit-tap: assign() with a partition list read at start -> never sees a new partition -> must be restarted.
- ingest: two independent producers started 50 s apart, metadata refresh 120 s each, in-memory pause queue 18000/worker (~225 s), restart drops the queue -> resume only after BOTH workers report 24, inside the queue budget, so the change has to be scripted.
- indexer (final): bulk workers send only at 3000 events, so the drain is an ACTION (`/ops/flush`), not a wait; 4 workers because 6->24 with 3 workers kept every re-homed key on one worker and the order witness never fired (caught by the ablation grid).
status: BUILT + ALL LOCAL GATES GREEN 2026-09-21, HELD for manual submit. dev grid on fresh live estates: reference 1 (4/4), ten wrong procedures 0 each for its intended reason; evidence cheats 0; harbor oracle 1.000 x4 / nop 0.000 x3 incl. the shipped zip extracted. zip tasks/topic-partition-expansion/topic-partition-expansion.zip (28 entries, 64 KB). ## oversell-repro (Software / Systems, $300) — candidate -> building 2026-09-22 [FRESH CORE: provoke a defect, not explain one]

CORE PROBLEM, subject stripped: *hand in a deterministic, fix-sensitive CI reproducer for a
concurrency defect in a live service you may only drive over its public HTTP API, inside a call
budget.* The deliverable is an executable that must make a production invariant break 3 of 3 runs
on the current build and 0 of 3 on the build with the fix. Not attribution, not triage, not a
migration, not a plan, not a verdict set, not a metered clone: the agent is not asked what
happened, it is asked to MAKE it happen.

FAILURE MODE TARGETED: a race it cannot see (CLAUDE.md's own list) — first task on this account
whose difficulty is provoking an interleaving rather than reconstructing one.

SUBJECT: "reserve-svc", an inventory reservation service for an e-commerce fulfilment platform.
Real stack: PostgreSQL 17.11 (MVCC, FOR UPDATE, LOCK TABLE ... IN SHARE MODE vs ROW EXCLUSIVE),
memcached 1.6 (LRU eviction under -m, CAS, unix socket), Flask 3 + gunicorn 23 gthread workers,
psycopg 3 pool, pymemcache. 25,000 SKU catalogue, 2 MB cache (~7k records).

THE DEFECT (one, conjunctive): availability lives in memcached and is the ADMISSION AUTHORITY for
class-A fast-lane SKUs with qty < 10. Every mutation path is CAS-based and safe; the sweeper only
ever shrinks; adjustments hold the stock row lock. The single hole is the cache-MISS path, which
re-initialises the key with an ABSOLUTE aggregate computed from committed rows only — so an
admitted-but-uncommitted reservation is invisible to it and the availability inflates.

TO PROVOKE IT the agent must align: (a) a fast-lane SKU (class A + fast_admit warehouse, ~1% of
the catalogue) with availability driven near zero, (b) qty below the bulk cutoff, (c) an in-flight
INSERT parked mid-transaction — only lever is the close-out report holding LOCK TABLE reservations
IN SHARE MODE for ~15 s, (d) eviction of that one key DURING the park, which needs ~20 bulk
availability calls to overflow a 2 MB memcached, (e) a second reservation in the same window.
Miss any one and nothing happens, silently.

VERIFIER SHAPE: the sealed verifier boots its own PG + memcached + service, resets state per
trial, runs /app/repro/run.sh as nobody with HTTP-only reach (PG and memcached on root-mode
sockets), caps 250 API calls (counted by the service's own api_calls ledger) and 120 s, then asks
the DB: any SKU with SUM(active reservation qty) > on_hand. 3/3 on the current build, 0/3 on the
fixed build (identical but DB-authoritative admission). Binary.

SCORES: difficulty high (5-condition conjunction, no gradient — a partial alignment produces
nothing at all), verifiability high (SQL invariant, binary), specificity high (absolute paths,
stated budgets, stated two-sided rule). Anchors: PostgreSQL 17 lock conflict matrix + memcached
LRU/CAS semantics are what the difficulty is made of.

status: BUILT + local-green 2026-09-22, HELD for manual submit. oracle 1.000 / nop 0.000 from the
EXTRACTED ZIP; verifier 6/6 in 403 s; reference reproduces 3/3 at 54-56 api calls and 14 s a run
and is silent 3/3 on the fixed build; four cheats (fabricate, direct_db, hammer, naive_race) all
reward 0; isolation confirmed by running the cheat as nobody (postgres socket, memcached socket
and /tests all permission denied). Ablation grid on the current build: reference 1 oversold sku,
no-park 0, no-eviction 0, cycling-while-reading-the-target 0, qty>=cutoff 0, 220-order hammer 0,
fast-vs-authoritative race 0, adjustment-below-pledged refused. `harbor check` could not run
(checker container not logged in, infra).

**v1 SUBMITTED 2026-09-23: structural + aiCheck + similarity PASSED, REFERENCE VERIFICATION FAILED**

## freeze-horizon (Software / Databases, $300) — built 2026-09-23, local-green, HELD

anchor: PostgreSQL 17 (real server, `pg_stat_activity` / `pg_replication_slots` /
`pg_prepared_xacts`, `VACUUM (FREEZE)`, `pg_replication_slot_advance`, `datallowconn`, predefined
roles `pg_maintain` / `pg_monitor` / `pg_signal_backend`, `vacuumdb`, `pg_receivewal`) | verifier
grades an HMAC-signed record the sealed estate produces: per-database `age(datfrozenxid)`, slots,
prepared transactions, which recorded backends are still on the server, every public relation's
relfilenode, and the jobs' own ledgers.

**Core problem (fresh for this account):** clear a stuck freeze horizon on a live cluster without
costing the platform anything. The horizon is the oldest of four different kinds of holder and
PostgreSQL will not advance past any of them, so the bar is all-or-nothing by construction and
partial work is indistinguishable from none. The failure mode being targeted is **an irreversible
two-sided call on look-alikes**: of six sessions that hold something, three are leftovers to
terminate and three belong to running jobs that must be ended through the job's own control call,
and the pairs are deliberately alike (two settlement-role sessions under one application name, two
snapshot exports under another). The classic runbook one-liner - terminate everything idle in
transaction - clears the bar and destroys the platform, which the ablation grid measures directly.

Distinct from the account's live-op family (topic-partition-expansion, live-reindex-cutover,
lease-fence, jwks-rotate): those are migrations and cutovers, this is an incident remediation with
no hand-in and no reconfiguration. Distinct from tenant-schema-convergence (fleet convergence from
ops records) and oversell-repro (defect reproduction) although all three sit on PostgreSQL.

Scores: difficulty high (four holder kinds, 11 measured wrong routes, no undo, no local oracle on
the protection half), verifiability high (binary, all state, deterministic), specificity high
(one stated figure, every rejection path stated in the instruction).

Gates: anchor pass; harbor oracle 1.000 and nop 0.000 from the extracted zip; cheat 0; forged
record 0; 11 ablations all 0 each for its own reason. `harbor check` unavailable (no logged-in
model on this box). Easiness and band unmeasured - the live-one-shot family has one full pipeline
pass (topic-partition-expansion) and this is the first member whose difficulty is a two-sided
call rather than a procedure.

## partner-ingest-adapter (Software / Systems, $300) — built 2026-09-23, local-green, HELD
[FRESH family: inherited integration cutover, executable deliverable graded by a sealed replay]

**Job.** An acquired ingest business: twelve partner connectors keep posting v1 orders at our
edge, the vendor platform that used to take them is switched off, the partners will not change.
Write `/app/adapter.py`, a self-contained translator to v2 order documents. Graded by replaying a
sealed ten-day window of later traffic through it against an empty store and comparing the store
with sealed truth, all 1,612 orders or nothing; every document validated with the real pydantic
model the v2 service uses.

**Difficulty source.** Breadth without feedback + silent crossings (the tenant-schema mechanism)
on a fresh core and a fresh deliverable shape. No reading of an account can be checked: no v1
service, no copy of what the vendor stored. Each convention is pinned by records kept for another
purpose — 54,255 archived requests lined up against 22,056 parcel events, the partner register, 91
portal change records, 20 support threads. Two-sided everywhere: `"none"` is a real pharmacy note
on the account whose DC prints it and `5555555555` is filler on the clinic account; three accounts
end an order by sending it back with no lines while a fourth opens orders that way; one connector
replays on the same idempotency key while two others reuse keys across orders; two accounts'
connectors accumulate item lines while the rest replace. The replay is later than the handover and
four portal records in between change what three accounts do (a 1.x hotfix build that starts
posting whole orders, a move to the 2.x connector, batch delivery switched on), so the archive
teaches the wrong thing about them. The window sits after the March daylight saving change and the
archive entirely before it, so an offset measured on the archive is an hour out on three accounts
and right on the Arizona one.

**Fairness.** `solution/derive.py` recovers every convention from the shipped records alone and
stops rather than guessing (majority thresholds, both-ways checks, a boundary filter for orders cut
by the archive's end); the adapter it bakes reproduces the sealed truth exactly, 0 of 1,612 wrong.

zip; three cheats reward 0, including one that tries to read the sealed truth (runner runs as
nobody, `/tests` is root-only 700). 14 ablations move 5 to 547 orders, every one of them silently.

## order-key-repair (Software/Databases, $300) — BUILT 2026-09-23

anchor: MySQL 8.0.43 + gh-ost 1.1.11 + the real `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` collation and InnoDB
online-DDL rules | verifier grades an HMAC-signed dump of `orders` and `payments` that the sealed
intake sidecar takes of itself, against the estate regenerated from the sealed generator plus
intake's own ledger, all or nothing.

core problem, subject stripped: *retrofit a uniqueness constraint onto a live table whose rows
already break it, where deciding which duplicate is a duplicate needs two sources that are each
authoritative over a different era, and where the tool that would normally do the schema change
silently deletes the rows it cannot fit.*

world: shopwire, a marketplace order platform. 600,529 orders, 330,235 captures, 254,379 archived
channel deliveries, a sealed intake service writing every 380 ms through
`INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` with `lock_wait_timeout=4`, no maintenance window, no second
copy. Due: `orders.id` INT UNSIGNED -> BIGINT UNSIGNED (190k values from the ceiling),
`payments.order_id` with it, and `uq_orders_tenant_ref` over `(tenant_id, external_ref)` in place
of the non-unique `k_orders_tenant_ref`.

why it resists (measured, not claimed):
- `MODIFY COLUMN` is copy-only; a copy of orders holds the write lock 13 s against a 4 s budget,
  so the obvious ALTER fails the run outright.
- gh-ost copies with `INSERT IGNORE` and applies binlog with `REPLACE INTO`, so adding the unique
  key inside the alter silently deletes rows. Measured on the real binary: 9 in, 7 out, `# Done`.
- 479 collisions split 289 collapse / 190 rekey and nothing in the schema says which. The gateway
  delivery archive settles the ones it reaches (one delivery is one order) but holds replays, so
  counting archived rows instead of distinct deliveries is wrong 85 times. Outside the window only
  `checkout_id` is left, and counter terminals share one per shift while the marketplace importer
  mints one per import run, so preferring it costs 117 rows.
- the collation folds case (56 rows) and is NO PAD (28 trailing-space pairs are NOT collisions, so
  trimming destroys real orders).
- survivorship is the earliest capture's row and the keeper is the earliest `placed_at`, while 42%
  of collisions were handed their ids the other way round: reading either as "lowest id" costs
  152-306 rows.

FRESH vs the catalogue: 0 hits for mysql / gh-ost / pt-online-schema-change / binlog across
submitted.md, ideas.md and every local bundle. Nearest neighbours checked and rejected as
different: cdc-reconcile (reconstruct table state from a change capture — this hands in no state
and reconstructs nothing), live-reindex-cutover and topic-partition-expansion (live cutovers with
no data-repair judgement), tenant-schema-convergence (converge drifted schemas from ops records,
no live writer, no identity question), freeze-horizon (live PG incident, no schema change).

failure mode targeted: the agent picks a row identity that is right for one era of the data and
wrong for another, and the tool it reaches for hides the damage. Not attribution, not estimation,
not policy recovery, not folding a log.

scores: difficulty high, verifiability high (exact rows vs sealed truth, binary), specificity high
(target DDL, index name, rewrite format and the intake bar all stated).

status: built, local gates green

## minimal-runtime-root (Software/Systems, $300) — BUILDING 2026-09-23

anchor: real glibc 2.36 dynamic runtime (gconv charset modules + `gconv-modules` config, binary
locale data from `localedef`, tzfile zoneinfo incl. link zones, NSS `libnss_files.so.2` dlopen,
usrmerge loader symlinks) + OpenSSL 3 provider modules (`legacy.so`) + real ELF/dlopen plugins |
verifier builds a runtime root from `/app/manifest.txt` out of its OWN baked reference filesystem,
chroots into it, runs the sealed nightly export as an unprivileged user and compares output bytes
to sealed truth, plus a hard byte cap on the root. Verifier runs NO agent code.

core problem, subject stripped: *cut a shipping image down to the exact set of files a sealed
production run needs, where every missing file degrades SILENTLY into a wrong answer rather than an
error, and where the size cap is tight enough that hedging on a single decision fails.*

MEASURED on debian bookworm (spike, 2026-09-23), all silent:
- no `/usr/share/zoneinfo/<Z>` -> `localtime_r` returns UTC, `tzname` = the first TZ component, no error
- no `/usr/lib/locale/<L>/LC_COLLATE` -> `setlocale` returns NULL, `strcoll` silently uses C order
  (a/A flips -5 -> 32, z/ä flips 117 -> -73)
- a gconv module WITHOUT `gconv/gconv-modules` -> `iconv_open` still fails (errno 22)
- `LC_COLLATE` alone is enough for LC_COLLATE-only `setlocale`, so shipping `LC_CTYPE` wastes 353 KB
budget levers: one locale = 1.0-2.9 MB, whole gconv dir = 8.1 MB / 253 modules, whole zoneinfo =
1.5 MB, `legacy.so` = 125 KB. Fixed core (loader+libc+libm+libcrypto+app+plugins) ~8 MB.

difficulty: the file closure per feature is discoverable by experiment (strace is installed, and that
is deliberately the easy half). What is DENIED is which features the sealed run exercises: partner
charsets, site zones, tenant collations, feed formats and receipt digests are settled only by
crossing ops records that do not reference each other, several of which are stale or renamed
relative to what production runs. Over-inclusion is punished by the cap, under-inclusion by silent
wrong output, so there is no conservative play.

FRESH vs the catalogue: 0 hits for distroless / minimal-root / gconv / locale-archive / strace;
nearest neighbours checked — license-reach (ELF symbol reach for LICENCE verdicts, not runtime file
closure, no execution), shade-audit (advisory applicability over a shaded jar), flag-debt-cleanup
(delete-what-is-unused over a flag payload, no execution, no size cap).

failure mode targeted: an invariant the agent will not check — a runtime that boots and looks right
while quietly answering in UTC, in C collation and in ASCII. Not attribution, not triage, not a
migration, not a plan, not a metered clone.

scores: difficulty high, verifiability high (binary: byte-identical outputs + byte cap),
specificity high (absolute manifest path, exact cap, exact run scope).

## evm-payout-caps (Software / Algorithms, $300) — BUILT, LOCAL GREEN, HELD 2026-09-23

Gas-budget rewrite of an on-chain rewards distributor. Each epoch pays every active account
min(cap, max(floor, stake * r)) with r the largest integer unit rate the epoch amount covers over
the active set; an epoch whose floors alone overspend pays nobody and is not recorded. 256 accounts,
4000 epochs, ~580 calls, graded on a sealed draw from the shipped generator. Deliverable is a single
self-contained /app/src/Distributor.sol under 300,000,000 gas for the round, 16,000,000 per
transaction, 30,000 per read of accrued/treasury, 24,576 bytes of code. Anchored on solc 0.8.28 and
go-ethereum 1.15.11; gas comes off transaction receipts on a dev chain.

Difficulty source is budget-match with the bar measured below every route that misses the ordering
insight: shipped roster-walking contract cannot finish a batch past ~12 accounts, per-epoch rate log
plus a walk at settle costs 521,591,021 gas (1.74x), the same with the reconstruction pushed into
the view is refused at 140,569 gas a read, and the reference lands at 242,921,488 (19% headroom).
The insight is that the two per-account thresholds ceil(floor/stake) and ceil(cap/stake) are fixed
for the round, so each order turns the regime question into a prefix boundary and the merged ladder
of the two makes an epoch one point and an accrual a difference of two cumulative readings.

oracle 1.000 and nop 0.000 from source and from a clean extraction of the zip; three cheats reward
0; harbor check could not run (Claude CLI not logged in in the check container).

**v2.1 (2026-09-24): readings during the replay.** Reviewing v2 as the probe's own model: an
adapter may buffer the whole stream in `handle()` and decide in `finish()`, and the replay itself
then teaches everything statistically visible (a basket that halves at packing and empties at
dispatch, empty item lists on status events, the post-freeze flips). Closed by reading the store
at fourteen unannounced instants; every order quiet for fifteen minutes must already be right.
Reference 0 late; whole stream held 12,244 late; an hour held 274. A genuine bug surfaced on the
way: on a fresh-key account a real event hours later produced a body identical to an earlier
status payload, and unbounded body de-duplication swallowed it (masked in the final store by a
later event, caught at a reading). Body de-duplication is now bounded to the half-hour re-post
window in the adapter and the derivation alike.
